cards.speaker: src_stranger
cards.text: A man in a good coat asks to buy the Keeper's house. Not rent. Buy. He names a sum that would keep the gate for a year, and does not say why.

left.label: Not for sale
left.outcome: He leaves his card. It has no name, only an Ardent address.

right.label: Ask what he'd pay for the study alone
right.outcome: He pauses a moment too long. "The house. Or nothing."

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: A boat of travelling players offers a free performance for the town in exchange for passage. Their play, they say, is about a canal. Everyone's plays are about a canal, this year.

left.label: Passage for a play
left.outcome: The play is bad and the town loves it. There is a Keeper in it who drowns.

right.label: Toll like anyone
right.outcome: They pay, and perform at the Reach for free, out of spite.

cards.speaker: hesse
cards.text: I'm writing a piece on the Keepers of Halfway. Nine in eighty years, and four didn't leave by the flight. Dray makes five. I'd like a quote about the chair. Anything. Even 'no comment' is a quote.

left.label: The chair is comfortable
left.outcome: KEEPER: 'THE CHAIR IS COMFORTABLE'. It is read as bravery or stupidity, by shore.

right.label: Ask about the four
right.outcome: "Drowned, drowned, run out, 'resigned'. You knew that." You did not.

cards.speaker: tobin
cards.text: In my day the Keeper at Lock 8, that's me, used to swap a keg with the Keeper at 9 every solstice. Nobody's done it since Dray. I've brought the keg. You've got nothing to swap. I know. Sit down.

left.label: Sit down
left.outcome: Three hours. Somewhere in the second, the Dry Year.

right.label: Another night
right.outcome: "There's fewer of those than you think, Keeper." He leaves the keg.

cards.speaker: stroud
cards.text: A boat from the east with a woman who says she is Dray's sister. Nobody knew he had one. She asks to see the study. Mirren has never heard of her. Neither, it seems, had he.

left.label: Let her see the study
left.outcome: She looks at the desk and touches nothing and leaves. Mirren watches from the door.

right.label: Family or not, no
right.outcome: She goes down the flight. Stroud, later: "She had his eyes. Or I wanted her to."

cards.speaker: src_stranger
cards.text: A drover wants to swim forty cattle across the pound rather than pay the ferry. Forty cattle in a canal. Crane is somewhere finding the schedule for livestock in water. Dace is laughing.

left.label: Swim them
left.outcome: Forty cattle cross. One tries the chamber. The town talks about it for a year.

right.label: The ferry, and the fee
right.outcome: He pays, furious. Crane arrives with the schedule too late and is desolate.

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: A boat with no name, no cargo and one passenger, who asks to go down the east flight 'before anyone from Sorrel asks'. He has coin, and the look of a man out of other things.

left.label: Down the flight, quietly
left.outcome: He goes. Two days later, Sorrel asks. You say nothing.

right.label: He waits with the rest
right.outcome: Solas's men are at the gate by evening. He does not run. He looks at you.

cards.speaker: hesse
cards.text: Sorrel says the summit Keeper is secretly Aldmere's man. Aldmere says you are Sorrel's. I could print both; it would be very funny. Or neither, for a favor.

left.label: Print both
left.outcome: Both shores are briefly united in being annoyed with you.

right.label: Neither; name the favor
right.outcome: "A seat on the first Jubilee boat. That's all. For now."

cards.speaker: tobin
cards.text: The Dry Year, since you ask. Pound went to the sills. Company said drought. Then men came up the west flight at night, forty of 'em, said they were dredging the reservoir. I looked. No dredgers. Picks.

left.label: Picks for what?
left.outcome: "Never found out. They went up the north bank and came down a month later, thin."

right.label: Drought does strange things
right.outcome: "It does. It doesn't hand out picks."

cards.speaker: stroud
cards.text: A bargee has a fever I have seen in the coalfield towns. If it is what I think, his boat must not go down the east flight. If not, I have ruined his season for nothing.

left.label: Hold the boat
left.outcome: It is what she thought. Three boats are held. Nobody dies.

right.label: Let him go; watch the town
right.outcome: The boat goes. Nothing happens. Stroud does not sleep for a week.

cards.speaker: src_stranger
cards.text: A child, alone, on the towpath, with a note pinned to her coat that says 'Halfway'. Nothing else. She does not speak. Hale would take her. Ilse would take her. The Company has a form.

left.label: The chapel
left.outcome: Hale takes her hand. The child speaks, eventually, in a Lowmere accent nobody recognizes.

right.label: The inn
right.outcome: Ilse takes her without a word and feeds her for a year.

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: A boat of Sorrel students on a walking tour want to see 'the famous sluice house'. Famous to whom, you ask. To a professor in Sorrel, they say, who lectures on it and has never seen it either.

left.label: Show them the door
left.outcome: They sketch a locked door. One asks why the straps are new.

right.label: There is nothing to see
right.outcome: They sketch the chapel instead. Vosk, somewhere, relaxes.

cards.speaker: hesse
cards.text: Scoop. The Company's Board has three seats empty and the Superintendent of Halfway has applied for one. Pell. On the Board. I'd like your reaction. I'd settle for your face.

left.label: He'd be good at it
left.outcome: "Diplomatic. I'll print 'supportive'." Pell is touched.

right.label: No comment
right.outcome: "'Keeper declines to support Superintendent.' That's the headline you've bought."

cards.speaker: tobin
cards.text: Dray sat where you're sitting and asked me the same question you're about to ask. I told him the same thing. Then he went and did something about it. I'm not sure I should tell you again.

left.label: Tell me
left.outcome: "The water don't come from the reservoirs. Never did. Ask the old woman at the Reach what it does come from."

right.label: Don't
right.outcome: "Sensible. He wasn't. I liked him for it."

cards.speaker: stroud
cards.text: You have a cough a month old and a color I do not like. The summit air is thin and the water cold. Go down to Aldmere for a week. The gate will not fall down.

left.label: Go down for a week
left.outcome: A week below. You come back with color and to a gate that did not fall down.

right.label: The gate needs its Keeper
right.outcome: "So Dray said. I attended him twice that year."

cards.speaker: src_stranger
cards.text: A Sorrel engineer, retired, asks to see the paddle gear 'for old times'. He worked on the Sorrel flight in Marrow's day. He is very old. He calls the pound 'the Quell' once, and corrects himself.

left.label: Ask about the Quell
left.outcome: "A river. West of here. Dried up. Long time ago." He will not say more.

right.label: Show him the gear
right.outcome: He weeps at the paddle gear. Engineers do, apparently.

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: A very fine Aldmere yacht, a lady aboard who does not give her name, asks passage west and offers a sum to have the Book say she went east.

left.label: The Book says east
left.outcome: The Book lies. The sum is large. Crane, weeks later, asks about a yacht.

right.label: The Book says what happened
right.outcome: She pays the ordinary toll and looks at you with something like respect.

cards.speaker: hesse
cards.text: A reader has sent the Courier a letter claiming a Halfway Keeper once found 'a door under the water'. Unsigned. Aldmere postmark. I don't print anonymous letters. I do show them to people who might know.

left.label: I know nothing of doors
left.outcome: "Everyone says that. It's the least interesting thing anyone says."

right.label: Let me see the hand
right.outcome: You have seen the hand. On a ciphered ledger.

cards.speaker: tobin
cards.text: I'm not long for it, Keeper. Stroud says so with her face. I've got a Company coat forty years old and a tankard and a story I never finished telling Dray. Which do you want?

left.label: The story
left.outcome: He tells it. It ends with men going into the hill and the pound rising the next spring.

right.label: The coat
right.outcome: "Sensible. Warmer than a story." It fits, almost.

cards.speaker: stroud
cards.text: Fennick has fainted at his key. Overwork and no food, he says. Fear, I say. He keeps asking whether Vosk has been to see me. Has something been happening on the wire I should know about?

left.label: Tell her what you know
left.outcome: She listens like a physician. "Then he needs rest, and you need care."

right.label: Nothing you should know
right.outcome: "I see. Then I shall treat the symptom."
